note: A DRAFT FOR THE ANALYST'S REVIEW. Nothing here is a grade until he has answered the sheet. `drafted` records rest on an opened source and are exactly what would be written if accepted. `recommended` entries are the drafting agent's own estimates with no source opened; an accepted one is written as a practitioner grade.

reason: Fifth of fourteen markets on hold IRR, 9.6%.
持有期IRR为9.6%，在十四个市场中排名第五。
55% of first-year revenue is secured, for ten years, by a capacity contract.
首年收入的55%由容量合同锁定，期限十年。

Planning permission must be granted before a grid application, so the application fee, the first stage payment and the capacity bond all fall after consent. The fee is about 0.3% of project cost; the other two have no sourced amount.
须先取得规划许可才能提出并网申请，因此申请费、第一阶段付款和容量保证金都发生在取得许可之后。申请费约为项目投资的0.3%；另外两项没有可查证的金额。
The regulator publishes the connection policy, the two batch dates a year, the fees and the time allowed to process a batch, and the operators publish each batch's results.
监管机构公布了并网政策、每年两个批次的截止日期、收费标准以及每个批次的处理时限，运营商也公布各批次的结果。
Connection offers are issued in two batches a year to projects that already hold planning permission, with no cap on the number of applications in a batch.
并网要约每年分两个批次发放，对象是已取得规划许可的项目，每批次的申请数量不设上限。

Since January 2025 an investor from outside the EU must notify an acquisition of control, or of more than 25%, worth EUR 2 million or more in a listed sector; a decision is due within 90 days of the screening notice, extendable to 135.
自2025年1月起，欧盟以外的投资者在所列行业取得控制权或超过25%的股权、且交易金额达200万欧元及以上的，须进行申报；自发出审查通知之日起90日内作出决定，可延长至135日。

The system-services arrangements are being replaced by competitive procurement, with go-live targeted for 2027 and a possible gap after the legacy contracts stop; capacity contracts already awarded are unaffected.
系统服务安排正被竞争性采购取代，目标于2027年上线，原有合同到期后可能出现空档；已授予的容量合同不受影响。

capitalAtRisk: The anchors pull two ways again. The share I can source, 0.30%, is under grade 5's line, but a capacity bond is required above 5 MW and its amount was not in the documents opened. Grade 3 is drafted on the clause that fits exactly: security posted only after consent is in hand.

The first stage payment is stated for distribution-connected generators as the greater of 10% of the connection cost, or the lesser of EUR 10,000 per MW and half the connection cost. At EUR 10,000 per MW that is EUR 500,000 on the reference project, which would take the sourced share to about 1.3%. I have not counted it because the connection cost is per project.
Flags for you to confirm: I have taken the first stage payment and the bond to fall before your investment decision.
The fee table is the distribution operator's. The transmission operator's site refused the fetch.
approvalTransparency: Grade 5 also wants the queue and available capacity public and outcomes appealable. Batch results are published; I opened no page on available capacity or on appeal.
gridScarcity: Grade 3's test is that a prepared project can expect an offer within one cycle. The decision removes the cap on applications and sets processing times of 12 to 18 months for other technologies; it says storage that is not co-located follows the non-RED III route. I did not open a batch result to see how much storage got offers. The dashboard scores grid connection, planning and congestion 48 of 100.
foreignEntry: The sector test is by reference to the EU screening regulation, Article 4(1)(a) to (e), which I did not open; critical infrastructure including energy is what commentary says it covers. The 135-day extension is the argument for grade 3. It applies to third-country investors, so an EU investor is outside it.
policyStability: From the decision profile, as re-read on 2026-10-10. I did not re-open the operator's page.
timeToRevenue: Nothing computed: no pathway. What the decision gives: planning permission first, then the next batch date (31 March or 30 September), then the operators' processing time. Left to you.
supplyChainOrigin: I opened no page that establishes an origin rule, and none that rules one out. Left to you.
demandGrowth: The register holds the statistics office's data-centre consumption series, which is metered use and not signed new load. I opened no operator forecast. Left to you.
saturation: A seed line only. No ratio is held. Left to you.
debtAvailability: No count of financings is held and I opened none. Left to you.
exitLiquidity: Nothing held and nothing opened. Left to you.
scaleRepeatability: Nothing held on headroom per reference project. Left to you.

timeToRevenue.why: Planning permission first, with judicial-review risk the dashboard scores, then the next half-yearly batch, then the operators' processing time, then the build. Level with Western Australia and Romania (2).

supplyChainOrigin.why: I know of no origin rule on storage here. Level with Finland and Great Britain (5); you graded Germany 3 and Romania 4, so set this where you set the EU markets.

demandGrowth.why: Data centres already take a fifth of metered demand by the statistics office's series, and new connections in the capital region are constrained. A step under Finland (5).

saturation.why: The dashboard scores system services 40 and pipeline saturation 45 of 100 on a small system. Level with Great Britain (2).

debtAvailability.why: A small market with a handful of disclosed financings, sized on capacity contracts. Level with Finland and Romania (3).

exitLiquidity.why: Some portfolio and project sales; thin by count. Level with Finland (3).

scaleRepeatability.why: A system peak near 6 GW: a second 50 MW project competes with the first for the same batch and the same service volumes. Level with Western Australia (2).
